title: device VM session disk 100% full; $HOME unusable for scratch
observed: df -h $HOME: /dev/sdc 9.8G size, 9.3G used, 0 Avail, 100% on /sessions. 'mkdir $HOME/tmp/spacetest' -> 'No space left on device'. du -sh /sessions/* sums to 1.9G (the passthrough mount), so the used space is other sessions' directories, unreadable and not freeable from here. The project folder itself is a passthrough with 245G free (df -h . -> /proc/self/fd/3 932G, 245G Avail). /tmp is on / (9.6G, 4.1G Avail) and writable: dd 100MiB ok.
expected: a writable $HOME on the VM, since bootstrap.sh clones into $HOME before copying to the mount
hypothesis: the /sessions disk is shared across desktop sessions on jaspc and was filled by other sessions; it is not this project's data

title: bootstrap.sh hardcodes $HOME for the clone scratch with no override
observed: bootstrap.sh line 150: local tmp="$HOME/dps2-clone-$$-$name" is the only $HOME use in the script (grep -n 'HOME|TMPDIR|/tmp' returns one hit). With $HOME full, stage clones cannot run. Workaround used in this run: prefix every bootstrap.sh call with HOME=/tmp/dps2-home (the script uses $HOME for nothing else; pip's cache and venv temp also follow HOME/TMPDIR).
expected: a --scratch/$TMPDIR-honouring scratch location, or a fallback when $HOME has no space
hypothesis: the v1 build wrote the clone into $HOME to dodge the mount's unlink problem (comment at line 148) and no fallback was needed because the VM disk was empty then
